text:
Marc Gatcomb went undrafted, worked through the ECHL and the AHL's Abbotsford Canucks, and played 88 games for the Islanders before landing in Vegas. In 19 games with the Golden Knights he has been what his profile says: a fast, heavy depth forward. He has 67 hits in about 10 and a half minutes a night, and his bursts of top speed rank in the 81st percentile.

The trouble is everything else. He has two points, none in his last 16 games, and our numbers say the chances have dried up along with the luck. At five on five, Vegas gets only 35% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, for and against) with him on the ice, about 21 points worse than the team does without him. His ice time has followed: four of his last five games came in under 10 minutes.

There is a case for patience. Evolving-Hockey, in a small sample last season, had opponents getting fewer chances with him out there (91st percentile), so this fall's numbers may owe something to linemates and deployment. We'd watch whether the minutes keep sliding, or whether he settles back in as the fourth line's forechecker.
headline: Marc Gatcomb's minutes are shrinking in Vegas
